examples.title: Volume of a triangular prism
examples.question: A triangular prism has a right-angled triangular cross-section with base $6$ cm and perpendicular height $4$ cm. The prism is $10$ cm long. Find its volume.
examples.solution:
**Key idea:** The volume of any right prism is $V = A_{\text{cross-section}} \times \text{length}$.

1. Find the area of the triangular cross-section:
$$A = \frac{1}{2} \times base \times height = \frac{1}{2} \times 6 \times 4 = 12 \text{ cm}^2$$
2. Multiply by the length of the prism:
$$V = 12 \times 10 = 120 \text{ cm}^3$$

**Answer:** $120 \text{ cm}^3$

examples.title: Volume of a trapezoidal prism
examples.question: A trapezoidal prism has a cross-section that is a trapezium with parallel sides of $5$ cm and $9$ cm, and a perpendicular height of $6$ cm. The prism has a length of $12$ cm. Find its volume.
examples.solution:
**Key idea:** Find the area of the trapezoidal cross-section first, then multiply by the length.

1. Find the area of the trapezoidal cross-section:
$$A = \frac{1}{2}(a + b) \times h = \frac{1}{2}(5 + 9) \times 6 = \frac{1}{2} \times 14 \times 6 = 42 \text{ cm}^2$$
2. Multiply by the length of the prism:
$$V = 42 \times 12 = 504 \text{ cm}^3$$

**Answer:** $504 \text{ cm}^3$

examples.title: Capacity of a swimming pool
examples.question: A swimming pool has a cross-section that is a trapezium. The pool is $1.2$ m deep at the shallow end and $2.0$ m deep at the deep end. The pool is $25$ m long and $10$ m wide. Water is filled to the top. How many litres of water does the pool hold? ($1 \text{ m}^3 = 1000 \text{ L}$)
examples.solution:
**Key idea:** Model the pool as a trapezoidal prism. Find the volume in cubic metres, then convert to litres.

1. Find the area of the trapezoidal cross-section (the side face, length $\times$ depth):
$$A = \frac{1}{2}(d_1 + d_2) \times l = \frac{1}{2}(1.2 + 2.0) \times 25 = \frac{1}{2} \times 3.2 \times 25 = 40 \text{ m}^2$$
2. Multiply by the width to get the volume:
$$V = 40 \times 10 = 400 \text{ m}^3$$
3. Convert to litres:
$$400 \times 1000 = 400\,000 \text{ L}$$

**Answer:** $400\,000$ L

mistakes.title: Using the wrong area formula for the cross-section
mistakes.wrong: Area of trapezium $= (a + b) \times h$ (forgetting to halve)
mistakes.fix: The correct formula is $A = \frac{1}{2}(a + b) \times h$. Always write the formula in full before substituting numbers, so you do not accidentally leave out the $\frac{1}{2}$.

mistakes.title: Multiplying the wrong dimension by the cross-section area
mistakes.wrong: Finding the area of a face that is not the cross-section, then multiplying by an incorrect dimension
mistakes.fix: Always identify the cross-section (the shape that stays the same all the way along the prism) first. The length you multiply by must be the dimension going perpendicular to that cross-section.

mistakes.title: Forgetting to convert units before calculating
mistakes.wrong: Mixing cm and m in the same calculation, e.g. $V = 40 \times 10 \text{ cm}$ when the other dimensions are in metres
mistakes.fix: Convert all lengths to the same unit before you start. If the answer needs to be in cm$^3$, convert everything to cm first; if in m$^3$, convert everything to m.

mistakes.title: Incorrect capacity conversion
mistakes.fix: Remember: $1 \text{ cm}^3 = 1 \text{ mL}$, $1000 \text{ cm}^3 = 1 \text{ L}$, and $1 \text{ m}^3 = 1000 \text{ L}$. Write these conversions at the top of your working as a reminder.

practice.question: A trapezoidal prism has a cross-section that is a trapezium with parallel sides of $8$ cm and $14$ cm, and a perpendicular height of $5$ cm. The prism has a length of $20$ cm. Find its volume.
practice.solution:
**Key idea:** Find the area of the trapezoidal cross-section, then multiply by the length of the prism.

1. Find the area of the trapezoidal cross-section:
$$A = \frac{1}{2}(a + b) \times h = \frac{1}{2}(8 + 14) \times 5 = \frac{1}{2} \times 22 \times 5 = 55 \text{ cm}^2$$
2. Multiply by the length of the prism:
$$V = 55 \times 20 = 1100 \text{ cm}^3$$

**Answer:** $1100 \text{ cm}^3$
